title: Round 10 / ECDLP-29: frontier exploration B (computation models, problem reformulations, learning)
question: Propose and cheaply test deliberately unconventional but sensible ideas toward faster ECDLP from computation models, reformulations of the problem statement, and data-driven/learning approaches not yet investigated by the lab.

claims: F-B1 (experimental; toy sizes, one encoding, one solver): Plain CDCL (Glucose4) on a bit-level circuit encoding of [k]P=Q for prime-order prime-field toy curves (n=5..10 bits) scales as conflicts ~ r^1.2 (18 solved runs, no censoring), and its cost is dominated by a key-entropy-independent floor (interval-DLP hint runs). No route below sqrt(r). Evidence: experiments/round10-frontier-b/sat_summary.txt, sat_*.jsonl.

F-B2 (experimental; toy sizes, two learner families): Logistic-regression and 1-hidden-layer MLP learners with coordinate bit and Fourier features show no better-than-majority prediction of any bit of k (or sign/mod labels) on held-out k, in 6 exhaustively enumerated toy groups (r=859..6607); controls (identity encoding, x-parity) are detected. Detection floor ~0.045-0.12. Evidence: experiments/round10-frontier-b/learn_summary.txt, learn_out.jsonl.

F-B3 (unproved; analytic sketch, no new claim): Speculative learn-then-decode (hidden-number/list-decoding) pipeline is information-theoretically polynomial in 1/eps given an eps-advantage bit oracle, but the oracle step is unsupported by F-B2. Evidence: analysis only.
next_action: PI: record F-B1/F-B2 as negative experimental results; optional low-cost follow-ups (structure-aware SAT encodings with x-only ladder/XOR-aware solver; larger-group learning with planted-leak calibration); write advice/amortization accounting as precise HYPs. No reviewed claim; independent review pending.
